Common-word data derived from fxsjy/jieba
Source: https://github.com/fxsjy/jieba/tree/67fa2e36e72f69d9134b8a1037b83fbb070b9775
Included Chinese words: length 1–4, frequency >=20; four-character idioms tagged i, frequency >=3. Other tagged idioms preserve the prior >=10 rule. Additional game vocabulary and plain-language learning explanations are project-authored in data/.

Idiom headword verification and classification reference: pwxcoo/chinese-xinhua
Source: https://github.com/pwxcoo/chinese-xinhua/tree/fe6d6c2e8baa82187f4c96bbe042e43f96c05666
Reference meanings were used to check headwords and inform classification. From the 2026-11-01 vocabulary review, selected explanations from this MIT-licensed corpus are also bundled as offline fallback definitions. Project-authored explanations take precedence. A segmentation POS tag alone does not establish idiom status; reference absence alone does not establish an error. See data/vocabulary-review.json and data/idiom-definitions.json.

Wordward offline tracing subset (2026-11-01)
Original stroke data: Hanzi Writer Data, derived from Make Me a Hanzi and Arphic Technology fonts.
Source: https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/tree/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c
Copyright (C) 1999 Arphic Technology Co., Ltd.
License: Arphic Public License. See the unaltered ARPHICPL.TXT distributed with the application.
76 original character records were selected and aggregated into glyph-strokes.json on the stated date; original stroke paths and medians are unchanged. This tracing data subset is freely available under the same Arphic Public License and is provided without warranty. The subset can be downloaded as glyph-strokes.json beside the application. Independent game source code and project-authored lessons are separate works.
